response.sql:
WITH scan_rates AS (
  SELECT si.riskeval,
         CAST(s.gbsize AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(s.spanmin, 0) AS gb_per_min
  FROM scans s
  JOIN sites si ON si.zoneregistry = s.zoneref
),
group_rates AS (
  SELECT riskeval, AVG(gb_per_min) AS rate
  FROM scan_rates
  GROUP BY riskeval
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS bench FROM group_rates
),
above AS (
  SELECT g.rate, g.rate - b.bench AS excess
  FROM group_rates g
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE g.rate > b.bench
)
SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate,
       AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark
FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: Scans join to sites on scans.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry as an inner join, so scans without a matching site are dropped.
A NULL riskeval is its own group. Empty or blank riskeval strings are treated as recorded values, not as missing.
A scan with spanmin of 0 has an undefined ratio, so it is treated as missing (NULLIF avoids division by zero). A NULL gbsize or spanmin is also treated as missing.
A group with no valid ratios has a NULL rate. It is excluded from the benchmark average and can never be strictly above the benchmark. If there is no benchmark, the query returns one row of NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat blank or whitespace-only riskeval values as missing, so they fall into the same no-status group as NULL.
